leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 configurations (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) name B036, optical lattice clocks, as the preferred prize, all with Katori and Ye as laureates. Shared ground: the magic-wavelength idea removes the trap as the limiting systematic, 10^-18-level performance has been reproduced by several laboratories, and the consequences (tests of gravitational redshift and constants, dark-matter searches, geodesy, the second) are concrete. Not shared: the citation wording differs (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce speak of development and 10^-18 uncertainty with fundamental tests; Lindroth and Olsson use 'invention'; Pearce adds the redefinition of the second), and all five attach the same main reservation, namely overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. Johansson and Pearce record that they moved to B036 as first choice after reading the opening ballots. Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson say the pending redefinition of the second should not delay a prize; Kroll and Pearce list it as an open question.

Eriksson and Mehlig prefer B022, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. They share the model-then-experiment argument (2011 continuum model, 2018 correlated insulators and superconductivity), the reproduction by many laboratories, and the view that Bistritzer must stay in the credit. Both name B036 as an alternative and concede it is the more mature case; Eriksson also lists B054 and Mehlig B046. They agree the discovery is recent and the pairing mechanism unresolved, and differ little from each other except that Mehlig describes the maturity objection as serious, while Eriksson treats it as a risk worth taking. Both cite Cao and other 2018 first authors as unavoidably excluded.

Danielsson alone prefers B012, IceCube and neutrino astronomy, with Halzen and Spiering, citing a new observational window and the diffuse astrophysical flux. He lists B036 and B055 as alternatives and says he would accept B036 as the cleaner case if the committee wants fully settled interpretation. Pearce ranked B012 first at opening and now lists it as an alternative; Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce each question source identification and allocation among Halzen, Spiering, the AMANDA and Baikal pioneers and the collaboration, so B012 has one explicit supporter in round 1.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members put forward a single-part prize. Five prefer B036, two prefer B022, and one prefers B012; no member lists more than one ballot ID in the preferred configuration.

B036 is the most widely preferred option and also appears among the alternatives of Eriksson and Mehlig, who prefer B022. Members do not disagree about the quality of the 10^-18 result or about its independent reproduction; the disagreement is whether it is distinct enough from earlier metrology prizes.
The Katori and Ye pairing was described by Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson as unusually clean among shortlisted candidates, and the credited names were the same in all five B036 configurations.
On B022, Eriksson and Mehlig agree that Bistritzer belongs in the credit alongside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and Mehlig withdrew his earlier two-name proposal.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks are a new class of many-atom standard or an incremental extension of the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all flag this; Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson argue the lattice clock is distinct, and Pearce asks whether that distinction can be written into a citation.

Whether B012 rests mainly on the diffuse flux, which is well established, while the source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) rest largely on IceCube alone (Danielsson, Pearce, Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth).

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated insulators in twisted bilayer graphene weaken B022 (Eriksson, Mehlig, Johansson), or whether the magic-angle flat band and the existence of the phases can be recognised separately from the mechanism, as Mehlig argues.

Whether instrument-led prizes (B036; B021, aberration correction, which only Olsson ranks first at opening) count as physics discovery, a point on which Johansson and Kroll accept the principle and Olsson declines to push her own B021.
attribution_disputes: B036: Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, and the PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN groups lie outside a Katori and Ye pairing. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Johansson say they cannot settle the priority history from the supplied names and rely on recollection.
B012: Halzen and Spiering are credited, but Danielsson, Pearce and Kroll flag Baikal and DUMAND pioneers, the AMANDA lineage and the analysts of a collaboration of hundreds.
B022: Cao and other first authors of the 2018 papers cannot be named under the three-person limit, and earlier twisted-graphene band theory is mentioned as a possible precursor (Eriksson, Mehlig).

B054 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp): Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce refer to omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (BHZ), whose prediction the HgTe experiment tested; Eriksson conceded the point to Johansson. No member prefers B054.
B021 and B044: Olsson raises Knut Urban's absence from B021 and Johansson and Kroll note Wallraff's absence from B044; neither is preferred by any member.
maturity_disputes: B036 is regarded as mature and reproduced, but members differ on whether the pending redefinition of the second should be awaited: Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson say it affects timing, not merit or attribution, while Kroll and Pearce leave it open.

B022 dates from 2018 for the decisive experiment and the pairing mechanism is open. Mehlig acknowledges B036 is older and better settled, and Johansson, who ranked B022 eighth at opening, cites the same maturity concern; Eriksson lists B054 and B036 as safer if the committee requires settled interpretation.

B012 is described by Danielsson as mature in discovery and technique but not in source astrophysics; Pearce would see it as more compelling in a few years, while Danielsson sees large discovery potential ahead.
B044 is described as very recent in effect, since the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits (Johansson), and it is not preferred by any member.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, close to superconducting-circuit groups, and Chalmers hosted 2025 circuit laureates; he would recuse himself on B044 if it advanced. No conflict apparent for B036.

Kroll: possible conflict on B007 (Rempe, Kimble, Lukin) because he works on rare-earth-crystal quantum memories, and would recuse or defer; Wallenberg Centre links to Chalmers bear on B044 and quantum-technology candidates. No tie to Katori, Ye, JILA or RIKEN.

Olsson: Fellow of the University of Tokyo since 2025, where Katori is based; no known collaboration, she does not believe recusal is needed but flags it. She also declares a microscopist's bias toward B021 and a Chalmers link to Johansson.
Lindroth: long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier and attosecond groups, no tie to B036, B022 or B046; she notes proximity to cold-atom work as an atomic theorist.

Pearce (chair): no conflict for B036; astroparticle and detector work (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur) makes me a field neighbour of B012 and B055 and I would flag that if either became the leading proposal.

Danielsson: scientific closeness to B055 through an interest in black holes, no personal connection. Eriksson and Mehlig: no specific conflict apparent; Mehlig shares a Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson, not bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee state, in citation text or in a rationale, what lattice clocks added beyond the 2005 frequency comb and 2012 single-quantum-system control prizes, so that B036 does not read as a continuation of recognised metrology? Johansson, the member who ranked B036 lowest at opening, should say whether Kroll's and Lindroth's answer settles his objection.

For B036, does the supplied record support exactly Katori and Ye, given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN contributions? Which member can check the archival priority record, and is a recollection-based answer sufficient?

Should the pending redefinition of the second influence the timing of B036, or is the demonstrated invention the only criterion? Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson lean to the latter; Kroll and Pearce have not resolved it.

For B022, is the committee willing to recognise the magic-angle flat band and the correlated and superconducting phases before the pairing mechanism is understood? Eriksson and Mehlig should say what finding, if any, would change that view.

For B022, is a three-name prize of MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer defensible given the exclusion of Cao and earlier twisted-graphene theory, and does Mehlig's concession on Bistritzer settle the allocation?

For B012, what independent confirmation of source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) exists, for example from KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD, and can two names represent the neutrino-telescope pioneers? Danielsson should say whether he would rank B012 above B036 if Baikal and DUMAND credit cannot be resolved.

Is there any combination or ordering that the five B036 supporters and the two B022 supporters could both accept, and what remaining objection would keep Eriksson or Mehlig from joining B036 as their listed alternative?
Should B054, B044, B046, B007 and B055, which appear only as alternatives or in discussion, be dropped from further consideration, or does any member wish to advance one of them in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality and not a consensus: five of eight explicitly prefer B036, two prefer B022 and one prefers B012, with no member listing a multi-part prize. The B036 support is consistent in names and arguments but all five supporters carry the same unresolved reservation (overlap with 2005 and 2012, and the priority history), and several members rely on recollection for that history. B022 supporters concede B036 is more mature; the B012 supporter concedes the allocation problem. Round 2 should resolve the novelty-versus-prior-prizes question and the attribution record for B036 before the committee compares it with B022 and B012. These are positions recorded in the files, not a ruling.
